newsitem.title: USA: Boeing, FlightSafety form airline training venture.
newsitem.headline: Boeing, FlightSafety form airline training venture.

text.p: Boeing Co. and FlightSafety International said Monday they will create a $200 million joint venture combining their commercial pilot and ground crew training operations.

FlightSafety, a unit of Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc., is the world's largest airline training company, training more than 50,000 pilots and maintenance technicians annually in more than 40 locations worldwide.
The new venture, which will be devoted exclusively to training commercial jet crews, will include 11 FlightSafety locations as well as Boeing's three-year-old training center in Seattle.
Larry Clarkson, president of Boeing Enterprises, said Boeing has been training 1,600 pilots annually and losing money doing it.
"We haven't looked at it as a business," he said in an interview. "It's been purely a service."
The training market has been growing even faster than the overall commercial aviation industry.
"With the efficiencies of FlightSafety, it gives us an opportunity to participate in the growth and to earn a reasonable return on our investment," Clarkson said.

Clarkson said the new venture also will offer greater convenience for pilots. For example, the company is building a training center in China, which will eliminate the need for Chinese pilots to come to Seattle for training on Boeing jets.
Boeing and FlightSafety will each contribute $100 million in assets, including a total of 36 flight simulators, to the new venture, called FlightSafety Boeing Training International.
The approximately 630 employees of Boeing's training operation will have to reapply for comparable jobs in the new company, which will offer signing incentives of up to $15,000.
